records.name: A Charter We Can Sign
records.description: Offer Erie an equal council with defined responsibilities, common courts and room for practical cooperation. Vincent may accept this constitution, ask to preside within strictly limited powers, or refuse. His chairmanship would require our explicit consent and convey no sovereignty over Eyrie. Iovinus must decide which shared powers he can honour after the congress has dispersed.
records.brief: Two equal council seats beneath a constitutional frame with a removable presiding lectern.

records.name: Officers at One Table
records.description: The shared staff will have to turn familiar suspicions into questions that can be answered on a map. Supply officers will compare their plans while signallers practise carrying a report across the old divide. Iovinus expects each officer to know what he can promise, and when he must ask the government whose troops he serves.
records.brief: Opposed field telephones connected over one jointly readable supply map.

records.name: Specifications Worth Sharing
records.description: The same replacement part should not require a different drawing on each side of the frontier. Put the charter's technical services to work comparing specifications and production methods. Shared services will help the participating workshops, while Eyrie's engineers gain an opportunity to develop their industrial knowledge. Useful cooperation can begin with a part that fits.
records.brief: Two workshop drawings with identical component geometry beneath a shared production gauge.

records.name: An Order to Give Back
records.description: The civilian workshops requisitioned for the frontier army have received their release orders. The command has refused to hand them over. Its officers invoke readiness, but the authority that allowed the requisitions also set their limits. Iovinus must enforce those limits against his own military establishment or protect it at the expense of the charter's credibility.
records.brief: A military padlock resisting a civilian workshop release key, a clear conflict of authority.

records.name: Defence by Agreement
records.description: The staff can draw a common plan, but it cannot promise another government's soldiers. Iovinus will put a defensive league before Erie, with duties clear enough to survive the first alarm at the frontier. Existing alliances must be respected, and Katrina will have to answer for Avian in her own name. The officers may prepare the maps while the governments consider the signatures.
records.brief: A defensive league signal lamp beside two independent dispatch cases awaiting assent.

records.name: The Workshops Return to Work
records.description: Returning a key is only the beginning. Civilian production needs usable premises, replacement equipment and workers who can plan beyond the next requisition notice. The works office will inspect what the army has returned and hear the owners' estimates. A workshop promised back must become a place where someone can earn a living again.
records.brief: A returned workshop key above repaired machinery and a civilian repair estimate.

records.name: A Border Without Emergency Orders
records.description: The army will still guard the country. Its task can become clearer now that every consignment, workshop and journey need not remain at its disposal. A dependable settlement gives Iovinus partners whose consent matters and soldiers whose authority has an agreed boundary. The frontier should be secure enough to let ordinary business proceed without asking headquarters for permission.
records.brief: An ordinary trade wagon passing an open frontier post while a sentry telescope faces outward.

records.name: Eyrie's Own Work
records.description: The shared settlement has failed. The refusal may have come before a ceasefire, before a treaty, or at the final congress; the government across the line may no longer be able to keep its word. None of that repairs a road in Eyrie. We will honour whatever agreements remain valid, without claiming ones that never existed, and turn the work of recovery towards our own country. Iovinus promised to seek security without conquest. A disappointing answer does not release him from that choice.
records.brief: A domestic road repair crew's tools beside a closed failed-congress case and an intact peace lantern.

records.name: The Last Campaign
records.description: Iovinus's officers promise a campaign that will finally make perpetual vigilance unnecessary. He understands the attraction, and how readily headquarters finds reasons to remain indispensable. Choosing their campaign closes the negotiated road with Erie. The duke must decide what Eyrie will take by force and what his own command will have to surrender afterwards, so that victory becomes more than the next mobilisation.
records.brief: A campaign drum beside a village workbench and an hourglass, the cost of another mobilisation.

records.name: Break the Rival Line
records.description: Eyrie's claim has not persuaded Erie to yield. Iovinus will prepare a demand backed by the prospect of war, accepting responsibility for a contest that ancestry alone cannot resolve. An existing peace must still be respected. The preparations provide grounds to fight the rival House; the decision to send the army remains a separate and deliberate act.
records.brief: A rival frontier line marked on a campaign board beside an unopened demand case.

records.name: Orders That Reach the Column
records.description: A good order arriving late may be less useful than a poor one already understood. Train liaison officers to carry the same picture of the field between headquarters, engineers and the marching columns. Practical work with signals will help Iovinus discover where his command's confidence outruns its knowledge, and give the troops a better chance of receiving instructions they can use.
records.brief: A dispatch satchel connecting a field telephone to marching-column map markers.

records.name: Keep the Columns Supplied
records.description: Quartermasters cannot feed a column with the assurance that another district ought to have sent its carts. Improve loading plans, transport maintenance and the means of reporting a shortage. The army's demands travel through villages and workshops before reaching a depot. Understanding that journey will matter when those same places ask what the end of the campaign has changed.
records.brief: A cargo-loading ramp with a maintained truck wheel and a shortage indicator tray.

records.name: Victory and the Garrison
records.description: The rival army has been defeated and the territorial peace established. Eyrie's officers can still name a reason to maintain emergency command in every district. Iovinus must decide whether to return ordinary administration and economic life to civilian hands or make military tutelage the basis of the settlement. Neither decision will settle the livelihoods waiting outside the headquarters gate.
records.brief: A garrison key poised between a civilian town door and a permanent military office.

records.name: Montague's Unsent Reply
records.description: Montague has an unfinished reply to an older letter from Rosaline, and a question for Iovinus: must private words still receive military approval? The answer will reach beyond this correspondence. Civilian post can carry knowledge and ordinary business at a continuing administrative cost. Command supervision will keep communications useful to headquarters while reminding every writer that an officer may be reading.
records.brief: An unfinished personal letter beneath a removable inspection shutter, with a civilian postbox nearby.

records.name: Dates for Coming Home
records.description: The end of emergency administration must have dates that a workshop or household can plan around. Publish a schedule for returning civilian premises and responsibilities, and prepare the building work that will make their use possible. Iovinus will have to accept demands arriving without the discipline of a military return, and answer people who are no longer awaiting his next command.
records.brief: A release calendar with dated geometric milestones beside returned workshop keys.

records.name: The District Commands
records.description: The garrison will remain an institution of government. Give district commanders permanent responsibilities for coordination, supply and readiness, with staff trained to make those responsibilities workable. Their competence may bring a dependable rhythm to the settlement. It will also carry military authority into decisions that inhabitants might otherwise have made without asking permission.
records.brief: A permanent district headquarters with a fixed radio mast and local supply cabinet.

records.name: The Work Waiting After War
records.description: Enough time has passed for the chosen order to encounter ordinary needs. Under civilian administration, returning reservists need instruction and premises before service can become a trade. Under military government, civilian repairs compete with the command's orders for machine time. Hear the workshop reports and decide who will bear the cost of the transition.
records.brief: A workshop machine divided between civilian repair tools and military production fixtures.

approved_visual_override.prompt: A single compact antique workshop bench lathe, painted game inventory icon. Muted green enamel machine body, grey iron bed, small copper handwheel. Squat compact silhouette with generous transparent margins. One isolated object, fully opaque machine, completely transparent exterior and gaps. No backdrop, glow, haze, shadow, lettering, border, logos or other objects. Hand-painted strategy-game asset readable at 99x86 pixels.
approved_visual_override.note: Approved neutral artwork supersedes the prior visual composition only; original description, target pins and gameplay are unchanged.
approved_visual_override.quality_history: Neutral v1/v2 failed visual/transparency QA, not moderation. Neutral v3 approved.

records.name: Useful Trades
records.description: A former soldier can bring patience, skill and confidence to a workshop without knowing how to operate its machinery. Expand civilian production and the industrial knowledge that sustains it. The programme must build on the answer already given to the returning reservists; a new building alone cannot make an unfunded promise of training disappear.
records.brief: A former soldier's field pack beneath a newly equipped apprentice lathe.

records.name: A Permanent District Staff
records.description: The military districts need more than a succession of temporary detachments. Establish permanent staff and workshops capable of maintaining the equipment their orders require. The arrangement will make command more dependable while binding industrial work closely to its needs. Civilian contracts, where authorised, will still have to find their place within that hierarchy.
records.brief: A military district repair shop integrated with a permanent command telephone station.

records.name: Registers for the Districts
records.description: A garrison report cannot replace a civil register. Iovinus orders the district staff to reconcile property records, tax rolls and transport maps so that the two duchies can be administered as a country rather than as an army's temporary possessions.
records.brief: A civil survey map replacing a garrison operations chart beneath a property registrar's ruler.
records.lore_notes: Historical ID is misleading: current name, description and electronics reward concern civil district registers, not an Avian border campaign.

records.name: Inspect the Working Day
records.description: A prepared parade tells Iovinus what a district can arrange for his arrival. An ordinary working day will tell him more about the order he has created. Examine deliveries and workshop schedules, then visit after the officials have had time to put his instructions into practice. The important question is what happens when nobody expects the duke to be watching.
records.brief: An inspection lantern illuminating ordinary depot shelves rather than parade equipment.

records.name: The Road That Stays Open
records.description: The road that carried the campaign now carries other journeys. Improve its future through the construction knowledge gathered in the settlement, and look at the habits taking root along it. Iovinus wanted a final victory. Its meaning will be found in whether travellers can leave an emergency behind, or merely pass from one permission to the next.
records.brief: A former campaign road carrying a civilian cart past an open checkpoint.

records.name: No Unfinished Frontier
records.description: Avian has chosen true neutrality rather than Intergigantes. Iovinus's officers regard its frontier as the last gap in Verenia; his civilian advisers hear the dangerous promise of one more campaign before peace. The duke will demand incorporation openly. That demand does not erase the settlement with Erie or the obligations of an existing pact.
records.brief: A fresh Avian campaign demand beside a frontier telescope and a civilian travel case.

records.name: Orders Beyond the Surrender
records.description: The garrison can secure a bridge; it cannot settle every dispute carried across it. Avian's clerks ask who will hear appeals, pay the workshops and release the requisitioned wagons. Iovinus must decide whether local institutions will bind his officers or a permanent commission will answer for them. A subject government asked to surrender its remaining powers will receive guarantees, not a second ultimatum disguised as consent.
records.brief: A bridge-guard key balanced against an Avian appeals box and a released wagon harness.

records.name: A Province, Not a Garrison
records.description: The last temporary supply office is ready to become a permanent workshop. Iovinus receives its estimate alongside the register of Avian petitions. The soldiers have done what a campaign can do; incorporation now rests on pay, law and repair. End the provisional administration without pretending that the settlement's obligations end with it.
records.brief: A temporary supply hut converted into a permanent workshop beside paid wages and petition tabs.

records.name: A Court with an Ending
records.description: Herzland's offices now answer to Verenia. Among the papers reaching our chancery are requests concerning the imperial household. Before anyone offers to govern in Grover's name, we must establish where he is and whether we can lawfully answer for his care. An undertaking to protect a sovereign must also say when our authority ends.
records.brief: A palace doorway opening onto a household inquiry desk with an unclaimed key.

records.name: The Household File
records.description: A portrait, a rumour and an old court allowance cannot tell us who lives behind a palace door. The household clerks will compare testimony with the surviving records and establish what has become of Grover. They owe the council an honest answer, even if that answer leaves the proposed regent without a ward.
records.brief: A magnifying glass over an indexed household record with separate unresolved evidence tabs; no assumed living or dead Grover.

records.name: Who May Be Heard
records.description: A court teaches through its doors as much as through its books. Some visitors arrive with polished speeches; others bring accounts that contradict the official history. We must decide whether Grover hears those disagreements himself or receives the account his advisers consider fit to place before him.
records.brief: An open court speaking trumpet beside a lesson book and a partly movable visitor screen.

records.name: The Inconvenient Petition
records.description: A petitioner has named someone whose support our government values. The evidence has passed through the same office that recorded our guarantees, and Grover has asked to hear the case. A judgement will teach him what our promises mean when keeping them becomes personally expensive.
records.brief: A petitioner's property key on justice scales opposite a court patron's service token.

records.name: The Capital's Registers
records.description: Griffenheim's clerks possess shelves of overlapping grants and obligations. Reconcile the capital's records with those of its surrounding districts, so that a household can discover which office must answer its claim. The regency needs an administration that will still make sense when another sovereign signs its orders.
records.brief: Two overlapping capital property diagrams reconciled under an archivist's straightedge.

records.name: Herzland's District Books
records.description: The capital's settlement must travel beyond its gates. District officers will compare their rolls, settle conflicting jurisdictions and recognise the inhabitants whom the new administration is meant to serve. Their books should describe a country ready to govern itself, not a collection of offices dependent on our court.
records.brief: A district register cabinet linked to outlying civic offices by a simple jurisdiction diagram.

records.name: Work for Verenia
records.description: Herzland cannot become the sole occupation of the Verenian government. Our own workshops need premises, equipment and orders that will survive the end of the regency. Investment at home gives the returning administration something more useful to offer than memories of the imperial court.
records.brief: A Verenian home workshop receiving a new machine while an imperial dispatch case rests aside.

records.name: The Meaning of Service
records.description: Grover has asked to examine the work behind a military report. Quartermasters would begin with depots, hospitals and the journey of a consignment. The territorial officers would begin with command, responsibility and the duty to answer for an order. Either education must include the moment when our own authority ceases.
records.brief: A military lesson model showing a depot-to-hospital supply route beside a command whistle.

records.name: The Articles of Succession
records.description: A promise to relinquish power deserves more than a place in a ceremonial speech. The articles will name the country Grover is to govern, the resources its government will receive and the limits of Verenia's continuing obligations. Our signatories must be prepared to honour them when the imperial seal passes to another hand.
records.brief: Two separate government keyrings laid beside a defined handover timetable and treasury allocation trays.

records.name: A Crown Made Ready
records.description: The crown is the simplest object to prepare. The harder work lies in the ministries, army offices and accounts that must answer to its wearer. Let those arrangements be completed now, so that adulthood and a secure peace can bring the promised transfer without another excuse from the regent's desk.
records.brief: A prepared sovereign's dais behind neatly arranged ministry keys and a transfer clock; omit crown pending canonical review.
records.lore_notes: The focus is institutional preparation for transfer. Crown deliberately omitted; any later inclusion must copy Grover's canonical tall-pointed coronet, never lilies.

records.name: The Civil Settlement
records.description: The people of Herzland require courts, workshops and a government that answers in its own name. The council may undertake that work without accepting an imperial regency. Grover's protection, if he is here, need not make his future the business of our state. Let the civil administration rest on the authority we are willing to exercise ourselves.
records.brief: A civilian council desk with a court key and workshop plan, independent of any dynastic throne.

records.name: The Emperor's Public Oath
records.description: Grover returns to a country whose future cannot be settled by his surname alone. Before the assembled deputies and household witnesses, he will bind the crown to the settlement that brought him home.
records.brief: A sovereign's oath lectern bounded by a constitutional frame, with public witness benches.

records.name: Open the Reconstruction Offices
records.description: The first petitions concern roofs, wages and workshops whose doors have remained shut since the fighting. Local engineers and elected councils must turn those petitions into work that families can see from their own streets.
records.brief: A repaired town roof above a reopened workshop door and a wage purse.

records.name: A Charter for the Crown
records.description: The imperial signature must have a place in the law, and the law must remain legible without it. Ministers, deputies and the sovereign will set out who answers for each decision and how a citizen may challenge it.
records.brief: A law book with a clear institutional diagram supporting a restrained sovereign's writing desk.

records.name: Across the Vereni Border
records.description: Verenia was Grover's home before it became his neighbour. Resident envoys and visiting scholars can preserve that familiarity between two independent governments, each responsible to its own people.
records.brief: Two independent embassy doorways facing a shared scholarly book chest across an open road.

records.name: The Workshops Reopen
records.description: A repaired factory needs more than a new sign above the gate. Apprentices, foregriffs and engineers will compare the methods that survived the war and train a generation able to improve upon them.
records.brief: An apprentice's tool rack beside a restored factory machine and a tested component.

records.name: Petitions Before Privilege
records.description: An ordinary household should not need an introduction at court to obtain a hearing. Provincial judges and public clerks will establish a route from the smallest petition to a reasoned answer, even when a powerful name stands on the other side.
records.brief: A provincial petition box connected by an appeal stair to accessible justice scales.

records.name: The Service Oath
records.description: Grover remembers the officers who taught him that command begins with responsibility. The army's new service articles will place the defence of the country under lawful civilian authority and give its soldiers a clear duty to the communities behind them.
records.brief: A defensive service sword secured beneath a civilian legal clasp beside a home-town gate.

records.name: A University of the Settlement
records.description: The rebuilt lecture halls will welcome students whose families once stood on opposite sides of the war. Public laboratories and open appointments can make the university a shared undertaking that outlasts the ceremonies of restoration.
records.brief: A rebuilt lecture hall arch framing a public laboratory instrument and two student satchels.

records.name: Provision the Home Army
records.description: Quartermasters have brought the ministry a practical list: reliable tools, sound equipment and workshops close enough to maintain them. The home army will be provisioned for the defence of the settlement and the people living within it.
records.brief: A home-defence arsenal rack with repair tools and a short supply-route diagram.

records.name: The Work of a Reign
records.description: The crown has returned to daily life. Its worth will be measured in hearings kept, classrooms opened and promises honoured when they become inconvenient. Grover must now learn to govern within the institutions he helped to establish.
records.brief: A palace clock above an ordinary courthouse key and an open classroom book, restoration becoming daily government.

records.name: The Language of the Schoolroom
records.description: A school inspector brings Vincent three exercise books: Aquileian prose, Griffish arithmetic, and a local song written as its singer speaks. All belong to Erie. Avian's language quarrel warns us what happens when the court mistakes its own speech for everyone's education. Our teachers must first count the children whom their lessons cannot reach.
records.brief: Three exercise books showing prose-line blocks, arithmetic counters and a musical phrase beneath an inspector's lens.

records.name: An Aquileian Curriculum
records.description: Erie's Aquileian inheritance can offer more than courtly manners. Affordable primers and a common written standard will connect village lessons to a substantial literature of science and history. Vincent will fund teacher training in Aquileian while keeping local speech welcome in the classroom. Cultural kinship gives our schools a direction; their administration remains Erie's responsibility.
records.brief: An affordable illustrated primer beside a teacher's lesson box, Aquileian education without imported heraldry.

records.name: Two Living Languages
records.description: An Aquileian-speaking child should not have to forget home to learn Griffish, nor should a Griffish-speaking child be excluded from Erie's public life. Parallel readers and teachers trained in both languages will make the first lesson comprehensible and the second language attainable. The extra expense buys a curriculum that more families can trust.
records.brief: Two parallel readers beneath one teaching lamp, equal bookmarks and matching lesson diagrams.

records.name: Journals Beyond the Court
records.description: Aquileian scientific journals too often end their journey on a noble's shelf. A public translation bureau will purchase subscriptions, explain unfamiliar terms, and circulate practical extracts among technical schools. Wireless theory and electrical measurement will become subjects our own students can investigate, rather than marvels reported from distant academies.
records.brief: A scientific journal with circuit diagrams passing through a translation desk toward a school instrument.

records.name: District Teacher Colleges
records.description: Printing two versions of a textbook cannot replace a teacher who understands both. District colleges will train instructors to explain arithmetic, mechanics, and electrical experiments across the language divide. Scholarships for village candidates will carry these methods home, while shared examinations let an apprentice continue studying beyond the district of their birth.
records.brief: A district teacher-college gate framing paired lesson slates and an electrical demonstration.

records.name: A Place for Local Histories
records.description: The school standard need not become the measure of every story. Town libraries will collect songs, family records, and testimony in the dialects in which they survive, with translations beside them. When a village finds its own history on a public shelf, the cultural settlement becomes something its inhabitants have helped to write.
records.brief: A village song cylinder beside a family-record binding and an open library shelf.

records.name: Scholarships in Public Trust
records.description: A capable pupil should not need a relative at Vincent's court to reach a laboratory. A permanent endowment will award scholarships through published examinations and require its scholars to teach or serve in public institutions. Erie's cultural choice will thus leave a durable inheritance: trained teachers, accessible learning, and researchers accountable to their own country.
records.brief: A public examination slate unlocking a scholarship chest beside a laboratory stool.

records.name: The Language of Public Service
records.description: Iovinus receives a petition from a parish teacher whose pupils can recite an imperial lesson but cannot explain it in their own words. Eyrie's offices face the same problem with recruits and clerks. Avian's argument over language belongs here too: the House must decide how its Herzland inheritance can become an education its people actually share.
records.brief: An imperial-style lesson book beside a pupil's unanswered arithmetic slate and a teacher's petition box.

records.name: The Herzland School Tradition
records.description: The imperial written tradition gives Eyrie access to generations of scholarship. A Griffish curriculum, supported by modern primers and trained teachers, will connect parish schools to that wider body of knowledge. Iovinus can honour the Herzland's intellectual inheritance through an independent school system, with lessons explained patiently wherever a local dialect remains the language of home.
records.brief: A Griffish primer connected by a bookmark to an older scholarly volume and parish school bell.

records.name: Two Living Languages
records.description: Eyrie's Griffish institutions can make room for Aquileian-speaking neighbours without abandoning their own inheritance. Bilingual readers and equal access to public examinations will let families approach the schoolhouse with confidence. Teachers will begin with the language a pupil knows and teach the other as an additional skill, preserving a shared civic life across the borderland's different voices.
records.brief: Two differently bound language readers sharing one public-examination abacus.

records.name: A Common Technical Lexicon
records.description: A workshop manual is of little use when every instructor gives a different name to the same part. Engineers and schoolmasters will prepare Griffish reference works from the Herzland's technical literature, with familiar local terms indexed alongside them. Consistent descriptions and tested examples will help Eyrie's workshops turn formal instruction into better industrial practice.
records.brief: An illustrated machine-parts lexicon beside a matching real gear and measuring caliper.

records.name: The College of Interpreters
records.description: Our bilingual settlement needs people who can carry a precise meaning between languages. The new college will train teachers, technical translators, and public interpreters through practical work with machines and instruments. Its graduates will make industrial manuals and electrical research usable on either side of a linguistic boundary, beginning with Eyrie's own schools.
records.brief: An interpreter's lectern holding paired technical diagrams beside a working electrical coil.

records.name: Open the Parish Archives
records.description: Registers and chronicles tell a richer story than the chancery's official histories alone. Parish archives will receive funds for conservation, public catalogues, and translations of records that younger readers can no longer understand. Keeping these voices accessible will let Eyrie's inhabitants recognise their communities within the House's cultural settlement.
records.brief: A conserved parish register in an archival cradle beside a catalogue drawer and recording quill.

records.name: Fellowships for Civic Service
records.description: Iovinus will establish fellowships for talented pupils from every district, awarded through public examinations. Their recipients will return as teachers, researchers, and trained civil servants. Whether their early lessons followed the Herzland standard or a bilingual reader, they will share the duty to make knowledge useful to the country that supported their studies.
records.brief: An examination score abacus beside a fellowship purse and a civic-service key.

records.name: The Griffenheim Settlement
records.description: The imperial attack on a signatory has ended in defeat, and the peace conference has left Griffenheim in our hands. Victory has brought responsibilities which the Verenia charter never expected. We may offer a limited civilian reconstruction mandate, with a public account of its work and a fixed end. The charter does not oblige us to accept an imperial crown.
records.brief: A temporary reconstruction office scaffold around a damaged civic gate, an expiry clock prominent.

records.name: The Household's Record
records.description: The fate of Grover VI cannot be settled by an inventory of the palace. Before writing a single dynastic clause, the commission must distinguish a living child from an adult, a confirmed death from an unverified report, and a household here from one sheltered elsewhere. Its report will confer no title or guardianship.
records.brief: An archival evidence cabinet with separate household-status tabs under a magnifier; no portrait, grave or guardianship claim.

records.name: Contracts for a Living City
records.description: Griffenheim needs workshops, roofs and functioning public services. The reconstruction commission can establish a civilian workshop in the city, or invest its effort in construction methods which municipal crews can use themselves. Contracts will be paid for as public works, never as rewards for a new imperial court.
records.brief: A municipal repair estimate diagram beside a factory roof model and paid building materials.

records.name: Open the Technical Archives
records.description: Behind the imperial seals are useful surveys, machine drawings and inspection records. Let civilian engineers catalogue them and publish the work that can restore production. Access to these papers carries no authority over the dynasty whose seals once protected them.
records.brief: An opened archive cabinet releasing machine drawings and survey instruments to a civilian workbench.

records.name: A Voluntary Technical Protocol
records.description: Surviving independent charter governments may share technical publications and workshop standards with us. Where a House has lawfully joined the unified country, its engineers instead ask the civilian council to authorize a domestic programme. Each proposal needs an explicit answer. Reconstruction can continue even if it is declined.
records.brief: Two separate technical dispatch cases connected by a shared component drawing, consent still explicit.

No frame, writing, logos, invented heraldry, crowns, flags, human anatomy or extra decorative objects. Documents have only the described geometric diagrams. Do not add weapons or combat scenes.
