records.name: Publish the Mandate's Accounts
records.description: The commission must account for the factories it commissioned, the papers it released and the staff it still keeps from ordinary service. A temporary administration cannot renew itself by declaring its own work indispensable. The municipal representatives will read its estimates before deciding whether another funded year justifies delaying the handover.
records.brief: A municipal audit table weighing repair invoices against a temporary office's running clock.

records.name: One Final Funded Year
records.description: The unfinished repairs have names and addresses in the commission's final estimate. One more year's appropriation will keep its crews and research office at work, with municipal officials learning the accounts they must inherit. The closing date will remain on the first page. A temporary mandate must end even when its engineers can still find something worth repairing.
records.brief: A final-year calendar beside funded repair tools and a closed extension clasp.

records.name: Return the Commission's Keys
records.description: The municipal offices are ready to receive the contracts, survey books and keys. The commission's engineers will leave their drawings with the people who must answer for the next repair. Ordinary administration will have fewer extraordinary powers and no special mandate to invoke when a workshop asks why its bill remains unpaid.
records.brief: A commission's keyring set on a municipal service counter beside retained engineering drawings.

records.name: What the Victory Leaves Us
records.description: The Empire attacked a member of our charter; Avian answered, and the peace has left Griffenheim in our keeping. Katrina knows how easily a victorious guardian becomes another master. Before the officers put away their maps, she will ask Iovinus and Vincent what a settlement in the Herzland must promise the Houses that survived the war.
records.brief: Three House consultation chairs around a damaged Herzland gate model, no claim to an imperial crown.

records.name: A Name Is Not a Household
records.description: Grover VI appears in petitions, inventories and proposed proclamations. None can tell Katrina whether a living child is actually in her care. Establish his circumstances before discussing guardianship. An adult needs no regent, a foreign household has its own responsibilities, and uncertainty must not be dressed as a death notice or an arrival.
records.brief: A household evidence file with a magnifying lens and separate age/location tabs; do not presume Grover's presence.

records.name: Orders for the City
records.description: A workshop in Griffenheim asks whether its next order will be paid in coin or another promise of national salvation. Katrina sends for the civilian estimates. Reopening productive work will give the city something more dependable than the arrival of a new banner; where premises cannot be opened, its engineers can still improve the methods of reconstruction.
records.brief: A Griffenheim workshop hatch receiving actual coins beside a civilian building estimate.

records.name: The Herzland Agreement
records.description: The Houses' original peace must survive the settlement beyond Verenia. With Grover present as a living minor, Katrina can propose a regency ending at his majority; a civil compact offers another course. Each independent government must answer freely. A lawfully absorbed House instead debates the text through its own estates within the unified country. Incorporation supplies no automatic assent.
records.brief: Separate assent clasps around a Herzland agreement case, with an optional guardianship key kept outside.

records.name: A Place Among the Learners
records.description: The technical schools need tools, teachers and permission to question a confident answer. Bring workshop experience into their classrooms and share their discoveries with industry. If Grover is a child in our care, he should encounter that work himself. Public education has its own purpose whether or not a future monarch sits at a desk.
records.brief: A technical-school experiment bench with an open visitor stool and a questioning lesson diagram.

records.name: The Price of Readiness
records.description: Katrina's reservist system taught Avian the value of knowing who would answer a summons. Beyond Verenia, the council must decide how that service can be sustained. A common supply office would negotiate competing demands across the whole settlement. Territorial reserves would rely on officers and stores close to home. Iovinus wants to know who may call them out; Vincent wants to know who will pay when they do.
records.brief: A supply depot model opposite a local reserve kit, joined beneath a bounded service frame.

records.name: Let the Complaint Be Heard
records.description: A petition against the reconstruction office has reached the council. The petitioner is neither a courtier nor a convenient witness to our generosity. Give the complaint an ordinary hearing, even where it embarrasses Katrina's administration. A child learning government, if present, should see that a respectful bow does not oblige its author to withdraw an objection.
records.brief: A petition box set level with the host council's own office key on justice scales.

records.name: Streets Worth Coming Home To
records.description: Behind the repaired public facades, families still share damaged rooms and workshops wait for reliable access. Send construction specialists through the residential quarters with the engineers who learned their trade during the war. Their experience should now help make a staircase sound, a street passable and a delivery ordinary.
records.brief: A repaired residential staircase beside a paved delivery alley and a mason's level.

records.name: What the Houses Keep
records.description: The constitutional guarantees must protect Verenia's institutions when respecting them becomes inconvenient. Independent Houses keep their governments; constituent estates keep their charter rights within the unified country. The courts, agreed obligations and limits bind Katrina's administration in either case.
records.brief: Protected local court keys within a constitutional frame surrounding the central office key.

records.name: The Date on the Last Page
records.description: A regency has an ending even when its guardians still have unfinished business. Grover's majority ends their authority over a minor. Under the agreed settlement he may become constitutional head of the Avian-Herzland state, bound by Verenia's reserved institutions. Neither unfinished lessons nor an inconvenient birthday can justify prolonging childhood by decree.
records.brief: A guardianship hourglass nearly emptied beside a key leaving its temporary lock; no perpetual child imagery.
records.lore_notes: Minority ends at majority. The constitutional future here is not identical to the separate restored-Empire route.

records.name: A Union Without a Throne
records.description: The civil compact rests on the Houses' consent and the obligations they can answer for. If Grover's death is confirmed, it must acknowledge the loss without inventing a successor. Where he is adult, abroad or unaccounted for, it must respect those different circumstances. The work of governing can continue without claiming to speak through him.
records.brief: A civilian meeting table supporting public-service keys, with a vacant ceremonial seat set aside.

records.name: An Ordinary Border
records.description: The frontier should become a place where a carrier checks a destination, not where another proclamation begins. Complete the limited settlement of the Herzland and keep Verenia's Houses within their agreed constitutional relationship. A constitutional future or a civilian one must give those living here reasons to trust tomorrow's ordinary business.
records.brief: A carrier's destination marker beside a settled frontier bridge and ordinary market parcel.

records.name: The Verenian Convention
records.description: The River countries have shown how common work can become common government. Our Houses must write their own settlement. The House calling the convention will seek the constitutional presidency, but its delegates must explain how that office will answer to the country. Towns bring their customs and courts to the table; surviving governments bring powers they will not surrender on a promise alone.
records.brief: Several delegate chairs around a constituent table with a provisional presiding lectern.

records.name: One Customs Schedule
records.description: Merchants can cross a peaceful frontier and still pay for the same cargo twice. A common tariff must survive its first encounter with a laden wagon and two clerks trained to keep different accounts. The Houses will reconcile their schedules and receipts until a carrier can cross with papers that mean the same thing at either post.
records.brief: Two customs receipt grids merged into one tariff abacus beside a laden wagon.

records.name: Roads and Common Workshops
records.description: A bridge cannot stop where the survey changes its letterhead. Engineers from the participating districts will agree on loads, deliveries and maintenance. New civilian workshops give that agreement a place to be tested: the fittings ordered on one bank must reach the builders on the other before the river rises.
records.brief: Two bridge halves meeting over a river, their matching fittings supplied by a civilian workshop.

records.name: A Common Civil Service
records.description: The new offices must be paid for and given authority that a duke cannot revoke whenever a petition displeases him. Local titles and Avian's languages will remain legible in the common register. Rosaline and Montague's private correspondence supplies no mandate for an official marriage: institutions must rest on public articles.
records.brief: A common records cabinet with distinct language tabs and a publicly funded office key.

records.name: Orders in One Chain
records.description: Iovinus knows how easily a temporary headquarters becomes a permanent government. Vincent's household officers will also have to recognise orders carrying another district's signature. The common staff answers to the constitutional presidency and its published budget. Local service traditions continue within one command.
records.brief: A unified command telephone beneath a civilian budget lock, local service kits arranged below.

approved_visual_override.prompt: One isolated painted strategy game icon, compact and fully opaque objects, generous completely transparent margins and transparent gaps. Composition: One black bakelite telephone connected to a neat three-socket cable junction. Grey-green base and copper plugs. No insignia. No background color, no halo, no glow, no haze, no shadows, no backdrop. No lettering or heraldry. Readable at99x86.
approved_visual_override.note: Approved exact source and neutral composition supersede prior visual guidance only. Original description, native pins and gameplay remain unchanged.

records.name: The Final Articles
records.description: The delegates now have a customs service, public works, common offices and a staff to put under a single constitution. Their final signatures will have a different meaning from the invitation. Each remaining government must explicitly agree to cease being a separate country, transfer its forces and holdings, and accept the initiating House's presidency.
records.brief: A constitutional binding beside separate government keys waiting outside its final clasp.

records.name: The First Ordinary Budget
records.description: The ministries must now present the first ordinary budget of the united country. District representatives return with repair estimates and school registers instead of rival declarations of sovereignty. The president's signature will put the new state's promises against its revenues, and every district will want to see where its needs appear in the accounts.
records.brief: A first ordinary budget abacus funding a school model and a district repair beam.

records.name: The Victory Roll
records.description: The throne we demanded at Griffenheim was an objective, not an achievement. Before a new imperial title can be proclaimed, the Herzland must be held through settled ownership and effective government, directly or through our dependencies. Let the military and civil offices account for the country behind the victory announcements.
records.brief: An imperial campaign map checked against civic office keys and actual garrison supply crates.

records.name: The Imperial Coronation
records.description: Verenia already has its Kaiser. Griffonia has not yet received a Zypressen emperor. Prepare a separate coronation after the Herzland settlement, with a chancery capable of turning the new dignity into government. Neither the ceremony nor the conqueror's surname can supply the consent of every crown beyond the capital.
records.brief: A separate imperial ceremonial dais backed by a functioning chancery cabinet; omit unverified crown designs.
records.lore_notes: Separate imperial coronation after Herzland settlement. No verified Zypressen crown design supplied; use the ceremonial dais and chancery instead.

records.name: What the Registers Actually Say
records.description: The imperial archives contain useful knowledge alongside claims of succession. Separate technical records from court rumours, preserve the former household's documented circumstances and improve the means by which offices exchange information. An emperor who wishes to displace a dynasty need not pretend that a missing page proves whatever his courtiers wish to believe.
records.brief: A split archive drawer separating machine diagrams from indexed household evidence, under a careful lens.

records.name: The Crowns Bring Their Own Accounts
records.description: Our dynasty's dependent governments have treasuries, workshops and obligations of their own. Decide what to offer them: protected local administration with common technical work, or negotiated ministries directing agreed industrial and military business. Family loyalty can begin the conversation. It cannot determine the answer.
records.brief: Several independent treasury boxes arranged around an optional shared technical cabinet.

records.name: Freight Before Pageantry
records.description: Victory has left repair orders competing with the transport of food, machinery and troops. Support engineers and choose where to put the next effort: civilian workshops and better construction, or a permanent board coordinating infrastructure and supplies. An imperial procession cannot carry the freight its timetable displaces.
records.brief: A freight bridge under repair beside an engineer's kit and a dispatch scheduling wheel.

records.name: Commissions, Not Family Orders
records.description: The dynastic rulers have received a proposal for common ministries, and some have returned it with whole paragraphs crossed out. Their treasuries and councils have learned to govern since the conquests that placed them there. Trubach must negotiate with those institutions: a family connection may secure an audience, but it cannot supply the powers his chancery wants.
records.brief: A common ministry plan with visibly revised diagram sections beside separate negotiating chairs.

records.name: Arsenals and Workshops
records.description: The war ministry wants weapons that can be repaired with parts made beyond a single arsenal. Expand military production on securely administered land and bring industrial specialists together over common specifications. The dynasty's authority will travel farther if its equipment can survive the journey.
records.brief: A military production press producing interchangeable components beside a transport-ready parts crate.

records.name: An Exchange of Practical Knowledge
records.description: A common surname does not make every laboratory's instruments interchangeable. The colleges will exchange drawings and teachers with the crowns that signed the technical agreements. Their first task is to make a demonstration repeatable in another country's workshop. Later participants will bring their own apparatus, and their own questions about what the older partners have learned.
records.brief: Matching laboratory demonstrations on two separate college benches, a shared drawing between them.

records.name: The Muster and the Harvest
records.description: The staff's neat mobilisation calendar collides with the work that feeds its soldiers. Dependent rulers are asking what the next campaign will leave available at home. We must choose how to organise our own forces: a stronger permanent cadre with a heavier domestic burden, or limited rotations supported by better training and supply.
records.brief: A mobilisation calendar colliding with a harvest sickle beside a limited-rotation clock.

records.name: The Western Approaches
records.description: Draw up the Aquileian campaign against the governments that now own the intended territories. The old names on a map may no longer name the states we face. Existing allies and dependent realms stand outside the new demands; the general staff must distinguish a frontier from a family possession.
records.brief: A westward campaign map with actual target boundaries and excluded allied areas, an unsheathed planning pointer.

approved_visual_override.prompt: One isolated painted strategy game icon, compact and fully opaque objects, generous completely transparent margins and transparent gaps. Composition: A folded fictional inland road map with a broad route bending to the left, beside a simple compass. No real geography, text or battle symbols. Ivory paper, muted green roads, pewter compass. No background color, no halo, no glow, no haze, no shadows, no backdrop. No lettering or heraldry. Readable at99x86.
approved_visual_override.note: Approved exact source and neutral composition supersede prior visual guidance only. Original description, native pins and gameplay remain unchanged.

records.name: Contracts After the Columns
records.description: The western settlement needs more than the passage of military columns. Give civilian builders dependable contracts and develop construction methods that can turn a damaged district back into a working economy. Our own workshops must support that work without claiming ownership of a neighbour's industry.
records.brief: A damaged western street rebuilt with paid timber and a civilian contractor's tool box.

records.name: The Northern Routes
records.description: Once the western approaches are settled, prepare the routes towards Cloudbury, Vedina, Skyfall and Haukland. Staff work must follow current governments and possession, not the assumption that every old crown still rules. Agreements with allies remain agreements even when their lands appear on an imperial map.
records.brief: A north-pointing compass above a staged campaign route and a maintained transport depot.

records.name: The Southern Workshops
records.description: A settled north permits the staff to turn towards Wingbardy and the southern industrial realms. Their furnaces and workshops matter as much as their palaces. Prepare demands against their actual independent owners without treating the dependent crowns already serving our dynasty as another conquest to repeat.
records.brief: A south-pointing campaign arrow beside a furnace and industrial rail siding.

records.name: Beyond the Eastern Marches
records.description: The eastern marches lead towards Hellquill, Longsword, Lushi and the wider eastern principalities. Arrange this campaign only after the earlier theatres are settled. The emperor's ambition reaches across Griffonia; the staff's preparations must still proceed through real territories, maintained routes and governments capable of answering.
records.brief: An eastward sequence of supply waypoints beside a marching-route compass and packed provisions.

records.name: Seats for the Later Arrivals
records.description: The campaigns have enlarged the family of dependent crowns. Their new rulers arrive with officials, debts and local promises that the imperial chancery did not write. Trubach will offer them places beside the earlier signatories, with the same need to agree on which powers belong at home and which can be entrusted to common institutions.
records.brief: An additional negotiating chair beside an independent treasury key and a conditional shared-office clasp.

records.name: The Accounts After the Campaigns
records.description: The regional campaigns have reached a settlement, whether through imperial possession, dependent governments or allied arrangements. Review what our ministries actually control and what remains another government's responsibility. Stable production requires orders that survive the departure of the officer who first demanded them.
records.brief: Separate responsibility trays dividing owned, dependent and allied workshop orders beneath an audit lens.

records.name: One Dynasty, Many Countries
records.description: The imperial crown has acquired a continental task. Its success cannot be measured by calling every dependent government an office or every ally a subject. Consolidate the army's experience and practical support services while preserving an honest account of which powers were negotiated. A Zypressen future must be governed, not merely proclaimed.
records.brief: An imperial administration desk with bounded jurisdiction maps and an experienced field-service kit; no universal annexation imagery.

records.name: Reconstruction Office
records.description: This newly established office coordinates surveys, materials and repair crews. A common schedule helps limited resources reach the work that needs them.
records.brief: A repair scheduling wheel above a compact crate of sorted building materials.

records.name: Maintained Public Services
records.description: Regular inspections and dependable repair crews keep wells, dispensaries and public buildings in working order. Local services can now address routine problems before they become emergencies.
records.brief: A maintained water pump paired with a medicine shelf, a small inspection wrench below.

records.name: Common Workshop Standards
records.description: Shared measurements, inspection routines and apprentice training allow small workshops to fill larger orders with fewer costly mistakes.
records.brief: A fitted measuring gauge enclosing three identical workshop components.

records.name: Veterans in Skilled Work
records.description: A new placement scheme helps former soldiers find suitable trades. Their practical experience benefits workshop teams, while willing veterans pass useful skills to recruits.
records.brief: A service helmet hanging from an apprentice's vise, bridging veteran experience and civilian work.

records.name: Practical Education
records.description: Teacher courses and accessible lessons give more students the foundations needed for technical study. Researchers can draw on a growing pool of trained assistants.
records.brief: A teacher's illustrated lesson book supporting a compact scientific instrument.

records.name: Professional Officer Corps
records.description: Regular courses and field exercises give officers a common approach to training, administration and command.
records.brief: An officer's exercise baton crossing a tactical training slate.

records.name: Permanent Supply Service
records.description: Reliable inventories and transport schedules reduce waste and make it easier to sustain formations in the field.
records.brief: A tightly packed supply crate beneath an accurate delivery clock.

records.name: Integrated Army Staff
records.description: Commanders and specialist services plan together, test their procedures in joint exercises and pass the lessons on through regular training.
records.brief: A command switchboard connecting specialist-service map markers in one coordinated plan.

records.name: District Repair Crews
records.description: Locally organised crews and a common repair register help damaged buildings return to service sooner.
records.brief: A mason's repair kit beside a public-building maintenance register with a roof diagram.

records.name: Rural Investment
records.description: More dependable farm incomes support investment in processing plants and workshops, accelerating civilian factory construction.
records.brief: A grain-sale coin stack feeding a rural processing flywheel.

records.name: Practical Education
records.description: Evening study links basic education to technical work, giving researchers a wider pool of capable assistants.
records.brief: An evening-study lamp illuminating a technical gear diagram and arithmetic counters.

records.name: Skilled Reservists
records.description: Workshop placements and refresher training retain useful skills in civilian production and military service alike.
records.brief: A reserve cartridge belt coiled around a workshop spanner.

records.name: Field Engineer Cadres
records.description: Experienced engineers teach units to prepare defensive positions more quickly.
records.brief: A trench shovel cutting a clean defensive earthwork profile.

records.name: District Depot Service
records.description: Better inventories and delivery routines reduce the supplies consumed by our forces.
records.brief: A depot shelf with matching cargo-count counters and a sealed ration case.

records.name: Trained Observer Sections
records.description: Reliable patrol reporting and local observation improve the army's reconnaissance.
records.brief: A field telescope focused across a carefully sketched ridge.

records.name: Coordinated Field Signals
records.description: A common reporting network preserves the observers' reconnaissance advantage and improves the rate at which reserves reinforce battles.
records.brief: An observer's binoculars connected by signal wire to a reserve alarm bell.

records.name: The Common Translation Office
records.description: Professional translators maintain consistent versions of common records and technical documents. Their work strengthens confidence in administration and makes research more effective, while the continuing demands of the office consume political effort. Its remit concerns shared business, not the resolution of every linguistic or cultural dispute in Avian.
records.brief: A translator's desk lens joining two equivalent technical diagrams, a small administrative coin tray below.

records.name: Clerks Appointed by the Towns
records.description: Common business is explained and recorded through locally appointed clerks familiar to their communities. Their relationships strengthen stability and make it easier to organise political support. They provide a practical means of communication while Avian's broader cultural differences remain matters for further work.
records.brief: A local clerk's service window with familiar district keys and an indexed records drawer.

records.name: The Agreed Budget Protocol
records.description: Consenting treasuries have accepted a common accounting protocol. Coordinated work accelerates infrastructure construction and the growth of production efficiency, at a political cost to its participants. Avian requires at least one valid partner signature; each other House benefits only through its own assent. The protocol depends on Katrina's preserved three-House charter. Occupation pauses its benefits. War between the Houses, Katrina's replacement, the Second Winterfest Ball or a communist, loyalist or fascist political transition voids its signatures.
records.brief: Separate contribution trays feeding a shared infrastructure abacus through individually closed assent clasps.

records.name: The Unauthorised Emergency Levy
records.description: Katrina has allowed the administration to take supplies beyond the agreed obligations. The appropriation increases military output, but undermines stability and increases the burden of civilian goods. All charter benefits, including the common budget, are suspended. Avian must withdraw its exception; any unresolved breaches in Erie or Eyrie must also be settled before shared benefits return.
records.brief: A military supply hook lifting a civilian materials crate beyond a broken agreement lock.
records.lore_notes: Negative constitutional breach: military output rises at civilian and stability cost; shared charter benefits are suspended.

records.name: The Common Treasury
records.description: The common treasury directs funds towards works needed by the whole country, rather than only the former owner of a road.
records.brief: A common treasury vault funding a bridge beam and civilian factory wheel.

records.name: District Credit Associations
records.description: Local associations finance workshops and suppliers under shared accounting rules.
records.brief: A cooperative loan purse beside a supplier's raw-material bin and production gauge.

records.name: Common Civil Justice
records.description: The same case is heard under the same law, regardless of the coat of arms above the courthouse.
records.brief: One balanced scale standing above two identical courthouse thresholds.

records.name: District Self-Government Guarantees
records.description: Districts retain their institutions, but common civil rights take precedence over local custom.
records.brief: A common civil-rights lock protecting distinct district keyrings.

records.name: Municipal Housing and Water
records.description: Towns and rural communities maintain housing, wells and drains under common sanitary rules.
records.brief: A sound house roof above a connected well pipe and drainage channel.

records.name: Interchangeable Parts
records.description: Production drawings no longer cease to be useful beyond the workshop that made them.
records.brief: Two interchangeable machine couplings sliding together without a file.

records.name: The Verenian Standing Army
records.description: A common officer corps trains standing formations and maintains unified appointment rolls.
records.brief: A standing army's service bugle beside a precisely aligned formation of equipment lockers.

records.name: District Reserve Service
records.description: Reservists train near home, while shared depots and instructors connect the districts into a common defence system.
records.brief: A reserve kit stored beside a home gate and shared depot key.

records.name: The Verenian Audit Office
records.description: Auditing common expenditure no longer depends on the polite consent of the official who approved it.
records.brief: An audit lens inspecting an official's own expenditure abacus.

records.name: Emergency Hospital Wards
records.description: Beds have been found in rooms that were never meant to hold them. Medical supplies and assistance from across the border give Avian's exhausted surgeons time to treat the wounded and return recovering personnel to service. The emergency arrangement lasts 120 days.
records.brief: A field-hospital cot with fresh bandages and a medicine crate; a small hourglass signals temporary emergency service.
records.lore_notes: Temporary 120-day emergency arrangement; avoid a permanent nationwide health-service interpretation.

records.name: The House Holds Its Border
records.description: The answer to Avian's demand has reached the frontier posts. Officers prepare defensive positions and make certain that local orders can still be carried out without permission from Hallhaus. For 180 days, this heightened vigilance strengthens defence and speeds entrenchment.
records.brief: A frontier lookout shelter above newly dug defensive earthworks and a temporary watch clock.
records.lore_notes: Temporary 180-day defensive preparation, not territorial annexation.

records.name: Civilian Border Compact
records.description: Road crews, workshops and civilian carriers work to schedules recognised on both sides of the border. Each government retains its own authority. Cooperation provides §G+10%§! infrastructure construction speed and §G+5%§! factory output while the signed compact is operational. Capitulation suspends these benefits; war between the signatories, subjugation, disappearance or a change of Avian's political route requires a new agreement.
records.brief: Two independent border posts sharing a road-maintenance wheel and civilian cargo schedule.

records.name: Joint Frontier Inspections
records.description: Mixed patrols carry officers from both Houses along the same frontier. Neither command can dismiss an incident merely because the other side reported it. Escorts, inquiries and complaints require continuing attention from both courts. The arrangement serves the armistice and ends when a permanent treaty replaces it or the ceasefire itself breaks down. An inspector's presence gives no claim to another House's land.
records.brief: Paired patrol lanterns above a single inspected boundary stone; neither overruns the line.

records.name: Promises Entered in the Register
records.description: The duke has heard the petitioners in public. Their expectations steady the country, but answering them requires civilian resources that cannot simply be diverted elsewhere. The register remains open until the promised work is completed or the independent settlement discharges the programme.
records.brief: A public petition box tied to a household repair-material basket, promised resources visibly reserved.

records.name: Roads Worth Repairing
records.description: The treaty has given engineers and railway planners a reason to invest beyond the next alarm. Infrastructure and railway construction proceed more readily while the two Houses remain independent and their peace holds. These gains belong to the treaty and survive a disagreement over the charter.
records.brief: A repaired road branching into a new railway siding beneath a steady peace lantern.

records.name: The Common Courts
records.description: The charter gives disputes between the Houses an agreed hearing. Enforcing procedure costs the government some freedom of action, but a judgement that binds both courts makes daily life more predictable. These benefits depend on independence, a valid charter and respect for its rulings.
records.brief: Two independent court keys suspended equally beneath one binding judicial scale.

records.name: The Joint Planning Staff
records.description: Officers from the participating Houses share supply calculations and operational planning. Compatible procedures improve organisation and reduce supply consumption without dissolving the national armies. The staff's benefits cease when the charter is suspended or its conditions no longer hold.
records.brief: Two national map cases opening toward shared supply calculations and a field telephone.

records.name: A Presidency Bound by Charter
records.description: Vincent presides over the council's agreed business within the powers granted by its signatories. The office lends continuity and authority to government, but confers no sovereignty over Eyrie and no hereditary right to command its ruler. This institutional settlement replaces the ordinary common-court arrangement and is suspended if the charter is breached.
records.brief: A modest presiding chair enclosed by a clearly bounded council rail; no sovereign throne.

records.name: The Public Council
records.description: Civic delegates sit within an equal council, making local needs part of the common agenda. Their scrutiny slows the accumulation of political power, while broader confidence and coordinated civilian works strengthen stability and construction. The council replaces the ordinary common-court arrangement; its benefits require a charter respected by the rulers themselves.
records.brief: Equal civic chairs around a public works model, with an open scrutiny lens.

records.name: Shared Technical Services
records.description: Common specifications, accessible technical records and regular exchanges between workshops improve factory output and the growth of production efficiency. The offices serve the independent signatories together. Their benefits depend on the continued operation of the charter.
records.brief: A technical records drawer feeding matching parts into two separate workshop trays.

records.name: The Duke's Exception
records.description: Vincent has placed a personal undertaking above the common court's judgement. His immediate freedom to act has grown, but confidence in his promises has suffered. All charter benefits are suspended until he withdraws the exception and accepts the ruling. The friendship treaty itself remains in force while its conditions hold.
records.brief: A ducal key forcing open a judicial clasp beside an unbalanced scale.
records.lore_notes: Negative breach of common justice; the friendship treaty is distinct from suspended charter benefits.

records.name: Avian Provisional Administration
records.description: Appeals, public accounts and requisitions must be reconciled before the provisional frontier can disappear. The work consumes officials and construction capacity until incorporation is completed.
records.brief: An unfinished administrative bridge between two registers, with a clock and temporary barrier.

records.name: The Avian District Charter
records.description: Local courts and workshop contracts survive incorporation. They make rebuilding dependable, but petitions and appeals remain obligations the central government cannot simply dismiss.
records.brief: A local courthouse key securing a reconstruction contract board with a workshop plan.

records.name: The Avian Ducal Commission
records.description: A single commission coordinates workshops and military supply. Its orders are effective; its distance from the inhabitants remains a source of resentment.
records.brief: A commission's central order lever driving a workshop gear above a tense, closed civic gate.

records.name: The Obligations of the Campaign
records.description: Clear commitments to suppliers and supporters make mobilisation and planning faster. Maintaining them limits Vincent's political freedom: the campaign consumes promises as surely as provisions, and those who provide either expect to be remembered.
records.brief: A supply wagon harness tied to a credit chest and mobilisation clock.

records.name: Rights in Defeat
records.description: Local guarantees give the defeated districts grounds to trust reconstruction and resume building. Respecting their rights strengthens stability at the cost of some ducal freedom of action. These protections must withstand demands from the winners as well as complaints from the losers.
records.brief: A defeated district's undamaged property key protected beneath a legal arch.

records.name: The Ducal Commissioners
records.description: Vincent's commissioners coordinate military organisation and industrial output through direct authority. Their capacity to get work done comes with unrest among those expected to accept instructions without a comparable voice in making them.
records.brief: A ducal dispatch rod linking an arsenal and factory wheel above a closed petition hatch.

records.name: The Chartered Ducal Settlement
records.description: Vincent's rule over the settled districts is bound by their charters. Predictable obligations strengthen stability, construction and the economy of army supply while limiting his political discretion. This settlement concerns Erie and its defeated rival; it grants no authority over Avian.
records.brief: A ducal key restrained inside district charter clasps above an orderly supply crate.

records.name: The Consolidated Ducal Administration
records.description: A permanent central administration channels industrial work, military organisation and political authority through the duke. Vincent can make his decisions felt more strongly, but the governed districts remain uneasy about how little stands between his favour and their fortunes.
records.brief: One central administrative spindle driving factory and army gears, with a narrow civic-access slot.

records.name: The Patron's Reward
records.description: Vincent has rewarded wartime service with the contested estate. His fighting supporters draw confidence from that loyalty. Others see a government whose undertakings depend on which side of the audience chamber they can enter, weakening stability and consuming political authority.
records.brief: An estate key resting on a patron's campaign sword above a displaced claimant's closed case.

records.name: A Hearing Even Against the Victor
records.description: The estate claim must stand on evidence, including where it challenges the duke's patron. Greater confidence in property and government strengthens stability and the growth of production efficiency. Service to Erie remains an obligation for Erie to honour, without making another household its payment.
records.brief: An estate plan balanced impartially against a service token, both under the same measuring beam.

records.name: An Accountable Muster
records.description: The rolls are open to scrutiny beyond the barracks. Local records and service returns must agree, and missing entries require an answer. Reliable figures accelerate mobilisation and strengthen stability, while maintaining that accountability consumes a continuing share of the government's political effort.
records.brief: A muster counterboard checked against a village register and an actual service pack.

records.name: The Officers' Confidence
records.description: An army commission has taken responsibility for correcting the muster. Professional review improves training and organisation, strengthening the officers' confidence in their service. Keeping the inquiry within the army unsettles those whose objections remain outside the barracks gates, weakening public stability.
records.brief: An officer's training whistle above corrected military rolls, behind a closed barracks rail.

records.name: Civilian Scrutiny of Defence
records.description: Local representatives have a recognised place in reviewing the demands of defence. Better justified deliveries reduce supply consumption, while confidence in the procedure strengthens stability. Regular scrutiny requires political effort every day, including those when the frontier gives no immediate cause for alarm.
records.brief: A civilian scrutiny lens over a military requisition basket and its measured allocation.

records.name: A Command with Defined Responsibilities
records.description: The professional command is responsible for maintaining readiness within acknowledged limits. Clear responsibilities accelerate planning and improve army organisation. Officers must arrange their procedures accordingly, accepting that military competence includes knowing when an emergency power has expired.
records.brief: A planning compass bounded by a service-duty frame beside an organised command kit.

records.name: Requisitions Without Release
records.description: The duke has protected the command's refusal to return civilian workshops. Retaining their capacity increases military factory output, but undermines stability and increases the burden of civilian goods. All shared charter benefits are suspended. Withdrawing this order resolves Eyrie's breach; any separate Erie exception must also be settled before common benefits can return.
records.brief: A military chain retaining a civilian workshop wheel after its release key has arrived.
records.lore_notes: Military production gains come from refusing to release civilian workshops; depict coercion and suspended charter obligations.

records.name: The Civilian Release Schedule
records.description: Ordinary administration and economic responsibilities are returning to civilian hands. Greater confidence supports stability and civilian factory construction, while the army loses some of the organisational advantages of keeping the country on an emergency footing.
records.brief: A garrison lock opened beside civilian repair tools and a returning workshop key.

records.name: Military Tutelage of the Districts
records.description: Standing commands govern the settled districts. They strengthen army organisation and planning, but civilian life must support a costly military apparatus. The burden on consumer goods and the loss of public stability accompany the order Iovinus has chosen to retain.
records.brief: A permanent command tower rising over a constrained civilian provisions basket.

records.name: Post Beyond the Headquarters
records.description: Private civilian correspondence can circulate without a commander's countersignature. Knowledge travels more freely, improving research. Maintaining a reliable service outside military control requires continuing political attention.
records.brief: An unlocked civilian postbox carrying an illustrated scientific letter.

records.name: The Commander's Countersignature
records.description: The command continues to supervise correspondence. Its familiarity with the movement of information helps planning, while the knowledge that private words may be examined deepens public distrust and weakens stability.
records.brief: A private envelope held beneath a military inspection shutter and a planning compass.

records.name: Reservists Without a Trade
records.description: Civilian boards must absorb returning reservists without the promised central investment in training and capacity. Uncertain livelihoods weaken stability and slow civilian factory construction. A release order has provided freedom from one obligation without the means to begin another life.
records.brief: An unused apprentice stool beside a discharged soldier's pack and a closed workshop door.

records.name: The Army's First Claim on Production
records.description: Command reserves workshop time for military orders. Arms production benefits, while civilian factory construction falls behind. The government has chosen to satisfy readiness first and leave ordinary repairs and investment to compete for the hours that remain.
records.brief: A production scheduling wheel allocating its largest segment to shells, civilian repairs waiting below.

records.name: Civilian Contracts Under Military Rule
records.description: Negotiated contracts give civilian workshops a defined place within the military settlement. More dependable supply reduces waste and improves the growth of production efficiency. Maintaining the bargain costs continuing political effort and does not abolish the district commands.
records.brief: A negotiated machine-time dial beside a measured supply crate and a contract clasp.

records.name: A Limited Guardianship
records.description: The regency cares for Grover while administering Herzland in trust. Its authority carries an obligation to prepare a government that can stand without its guardians.
records.brief: A temporary household key beside a small school satchel and a reconstruction tool; guardianship, not ownership.

records.name: The Adult Sovereign's Transition
records.description: Grover has reached adulthood. The remaining work belongs to ministries, treaties and the restoration of peace; it confers no further right to direct his upbringing.
records.brief: A ministry handover key beside an adult-sized office chair and a peace timetable; no childhood symbols.
records.lore_notes: Adult sovereign transition, not continued childhood guardianship.

records.name: The Verenian-Imperial Market
records.description: Verenian workshops and Herzland buyers continue to trade under an agreement between independent governments. The old regency's accounts have become the records of a shared commercial undertaking.
records.brief: Two independent market gates connected by a laden trade cart and a technical parts case.

records.name: The Defence Compact
records.description: Verenia and the restored Empire prepare their defence as allies. Their staffs share responsibilities without making either government the other's guardian.
records.brief: Two allied field radios joined over a defensive route map, each retaining its own key.

records.name: The Open Court's Legacy
records.description: Grover remembers witnesses who were permitted to disagree with the court. The habit of hearing them has followed him into his own government.
records.brief: An open hearing-room door beside a lesson book and an unscreened speaking trumpet.

records.name: The Managed Court's Legacy
records.description: Grover learned to work through an orderly circle of advisers. Their discipline remains useful, and the voices outside that circle remain a question his own reign must answer.
records.brief: A tightly arranged adviser desk behind a controlled visitor screen, a closed outside book.

records.name: A Law Above Favour
records.description: An inconvenient judgement once bound the regent's own supporter. Grover carries that precedent into an imperial court whose friends must now discover that it binds them too.
records.brief: Justice scales holding a court patron's key at the same height as an ordinary house key.

records.name: The Patrons' Precedent
records.description: The regency protected a useful supporter when the law became inconvenient. Grover remembers both the loyalty that protection secured and the petitioner who left without an ordinary hearing.
records.brief: A patron's service sword shielding an estate key while a petition box remains closed.

records.name: Provincial Public Service
records.description: Local courts and reconstruction offices share a public record of contracts, claims and completed work. A stalled project has an office answerable for it, and a petitioner can follow its progress beyond the palace gates.
records.brief: A public project register with a building diagram beside a repair crew's accountable office key.

records.name: Institutions of the Settlement
records.description: The restored state rests on working institutions: workshops that train apprentices, laboratories that exchange their findings and ministries that can carry out a decision without waiting for another ceremony.
records.brief: A working laboratory meter linked to an apprentice machine bench and a civic dispatch drawer.

records.name: Aquileian Scholarly Tradition
records.description: Erie's schools use an Aquileian written standard to connect elementary teaching with scientific literature. Teacher training and accessible books give local students a firmer foundation for advanced study.
records.brief: An Aquileian illustrated school reader opening toward a scientific apparatus; no national heraldry.

records.name: Herzland Scholarly Tradition
records.description: Eyrie's Griffish curriculum draws on the Herzland's scholarly inheritance. Clear textbooks and trained instructors connect parish classrooms with technical and scientific study.
records.brief: A Griffish technical primer beside a parish classroom bell and a measuring instrument.

records.name: A Bilingual Public Education
records.description: Aquileian and Griffish share a place in public education. Training teachers in both languages takes resources, but gives more families confidence in the schools and more pupils access to further study.
records.brief: Two equally open language books beneath one school lamp, a modest teaching-expense purse below.

records.name: Public Scholarship Endowment
records.description: Scholarships awarded through open examinations support a continuing supply of teachers, researchers, and civil servants. Their obligation to serve public institutions turns educational opportunity into lasting civic capacity.
records.brief: An examination key opening an education endowment chest beside a teacher's satchel.

records.name: Griffenheim Reconstruction Commission
records.description: A temporary civilian commission coordinates repairs after the defensive war. Its staff consume political resources; its authority has a fixed expiry and rests on peace and Erie's actual control of Griffenheim.
records.brief: A temporary repair commission key attached to an expiry clock and a construction wrench.

records.name: The Commission's Final Year
records.description: A final funded year brings stronger repair teams and a small technical research office. Its political expense cannot be renewed indefinitely. At the deadline, peaceful reconstruction passes automatically to ordinary civilian services.
records.brief: A final-year calendar behind reinforced repair tools and a compact research meter.

records.name: Civilian Reconstruction Services
records.description: Published technical records and trained workshop crews continue serving the public after the temporary commission has closed. Their benefit lasts two years and carries no special political authority.
records.brief: A closed commission key case beside still-used workshop tools and published machine diagrams.
records.lore_notes: Two-year civilian benefit after the commission closes; no enduring extraordinary political mandate.

records.name: Verenia Technical Protocol
records.description: Consenting charter governments, or the authorized research offices of their legitimate unified successor, exchange engineering papers and production standards. The finite programme grants no territory or dynastic authority. Unified participation ends if the founding, charter or homeland conditions fail.
records.brief: Two consenting technical folios exchanging matching component diagrams across a timed clasp.

records.name: The Limited Regency
records.description: Erie and Eyrie have separately accepted guardianship of the living minor Grover VI in Avian. An independent House signs through its government; a lawfully absorbed House votes through its estates. Katrina governs within those limits. Majority, death or loss of the required conditions ends the authority to act; old signatures alone cannot sustain its benefits.
records.brief: Two distinct assent clasps protecting a minor's household key beneath a finite guardianship hourglass.

records.name: The Civil Herzland Compact
records.description: Erie and Eyrie have separately consented to a civilian settlement. Independent governments and the estates of lawfully absorbed Houses answer for their own undertakings. Repairs and infrastructure receive support while the charter, sovereign homeland and current consent remain valid.
records.brief: Separate civic assent keys supporting a repaired bridge arch and a municipal tool case.

records.name: Verenia's Constitutional Guarantees
records.description: The Houses' reserved institutions bind the settlement, including an adult constitutional monarch. Independent partners keep their governments; constituent estates retain their agreed voice within the unified country. Reliable obligations strengthen stability and production, while respecting them consumes political influence.
records.brief: District institutional keys protected inside an enduring constitutional bracket around a central office key.

records.name: The Joint Supply Offices
records.description: Agreed schedules and supply arrangements let Avian prepare plans faster and consume fewer supplies. Keeping the offices accountable to the settlement requires continuing political work. Their remit grants no command over an independent House's army.
records.brief: A jointly approved delivery clock connected to a ration crate and field planning compass.

records.name: The Territorial Reserve Articles
records.description: Reserves organised around familiar ground strengthen defence on our core territory and help formations recover. Planning proceeds more slowly as local readiness takes precedence over the convenience of a single timetable. The arrangement develops Katrina's reservist tradition within the agreed limits.
records.brief: A reserve kit beside a home-terrain earthwork and a recovery canteen.

records.name: Common Customs
records.description: One schedule and compatible industrial standards reduce duplicated work.
records.brief: One customs measuring bar aligning a cargo crate and standard machine component.

records.name: Interprovincial Works
records.description: Shared contracts keep workshops and roads useful across the former boundaries.
records.brief: A shared workshop order wheel connected to a repaired road section.

records.name: Building the Common Service
records.description: The new offices require political attention while they establish reliable common records.
records.brief: A growing common records cabinet beside a running administrative clock and a technical reference book.

records.name: Constitutional Joint Command
records.description: The shared staff serves the presidency while respecting local service traditions.
records.brief: A shared staff receiver beneath a civilian presidency lock, two local service cords preserved.

records.name: The Founded Verenian State
records.description: The founding administration joins industry and defence under one government. Its first ordinary budget is still being prepared.
records.brief: A newly joined government keyring beside an unfinished first-budget abacus and a factory wheel.

records.name: Verenian Common Institutions
records.description: Local customs and languages endure within one constitutional state. Working schools, offices, workshops and a unified staff give its presidency lasting substance.
records.brief: An operating civic clock linking a school bell and a supply depot, ordinary unified institutions.

records.name: The Imperial Chancery
records.description: A new imperial office lends stability and political authority to Trubach's coronation. It operates while his independent government and effective control of Griffenheim through Verenia or its subjects endure.
records.brief: An imperial chancery cabinet beside a stable ceremonial dais and a Griffenheim office key; no invented arms.

records.name: An Autonomous Dynastic Compact
records.description: This dependent government has accepted common technical work while retaining its own administration. Stable local orders favour civilian construction, at an ongoing political cost. No territory or sovereignty is transferred by the compact.
records.brief: An independently locked local treasury beside an accepted technical folio and a civilian building beam.

records.name: Negotiated Common Ministries
records.description: This government has expressly delegated agreed industrial and technical responsibilities to common ministries. Military production and research benefit, while the administration consumes political effort. Its crown, territory and existing subject relationship remain intact.
records.brief: Separate ministry keys engaging an agreed machine-production gear and laboratory circuit.

records.name: The Working Dynastic Network
records.description: At least one eligible crown has accepted an institutional agreement. Exchange accelerates research and production efficiency growth, with a political cost to the imperial government. Refusal by every partner leaves no network to administer.
records.brief: A dispatch exchange wheel linking two consenting technical cases and a production gauge.

records.name: The Freight Coordination Board
records.description: Permanent dispatchers coordinate infrastructure work and reduce the waste of military supplies. Their authority concerns our transport administration; they have not been given another crown's railways.
records.brief: A railway dispatch lever beside a track-maintenance plan and measured military cargo.

records.name: A Permanent Campaign Cadre
records.description: Standing officers and specialists improve organisation and planning. Maintaining this cadre strains domestic stability. The measure reorganises our own army and does not conscript a dependent country's forces by decree.
records.brief: A permanent officer kit rack above a planning clock and a strained household provisions basket.

records.name: Rotations the Districts Can Sustain
records.description: Limited rotations and practical training reduce the time needed to prepare our soldiers and the supplies they consume. The staff accepts a less ambitious standing commitment in exchange for dependable provision.
records.brief: A rotating service clock beside a compact training pack and carefully rationed supply case.

records.name: Orders That Outlast the Campaign
records.description: Predictable industrial orders support civilian construction and a higher production efficiency ceiling. The imperial administration is learning to purchase sustained output instead of treating every workshop as a temporary military store.
records.brief: A long-running industrial order drum feeding a civilian machine, with a stable production gauge.
